national_raw_news.title: 19 mins ago | National 110 Nation observes Partition Horrors Remembrance Day
national_raw_news.content: Today is Partition Horrors Remembrance Day. The nation is paying homage to all of those who sacrificed their lives and suffered unimaginable pain during the partition in 1947. Akashvani correspondent reports that, on Partition Horrors Remembrance Day, various programmes are being organised across the country, including in the National Capital. In a fitting tribute to all those who lost their lives due to the partition of the nation and were displaced from their roots, in 2021, the Government had decided to observe 14th August every year as the day to commemorate their sacrifice. It also ensures that future generations remember the pain and suffering endured by the people, as the birth of independent India was marked by the violent partition, which left lasting scars on millions. The Partition Horrors Remembrance Day keeps reminding people of the need to remove the poison of social divisions and disharmony and further strengthen the spirit of oneness, social harmony and human empowerment. The partition caused one of the largest migrations in human history, affecting about 20 million people. While celebrating independence, a grateful nation also salutes those people who had to sacrifice their lives in the frenzy of violence.

national_raw_news.title: 37 mins ago | Sports 25 Iga Swiatek beats Elena Rybakina to claim Women’s Singles title at Canadian Open Tennis
national_raw_news.content: In Canadian Open Tennis, seventh seed Iga Swiatek of Poland defeated second seed Elena Rybakina in straight sets to claim the Women’s Singles title in Toronto last night. Swiatek captured her first title of the season with a swift 6-2 6-3 win, giving her a confidence boost heading into the US Open. In Men’s Singles, American tennis player Ben Shelton won the title in Montreal by defeating fellow American Brandon Nakashima with a score of 6-3, 7-6(4). With this victory, the fifth-seeded Shelton successfully defended his tournament crown and captured his second career ATP Masters 1000 trophy. This victory marks his fourth tournament win of the 2026 season, following earlier titles in Dallas, Munich, and Stuttgart, bringing his total career tour-level titles to seven.

national_raw_news.title: PoJK protest becomes global
national_raw_news.content: The unrest in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK) has taken an international turn through protests by the Kashmiri diaspora to expose state-sponsored terror by the Pakistani establishment. In Belgium, Kashmiri diaspora groups today marched from the European Parliament toward the United Nations in Brussels, calling for international scrutiny of the situation in PoJK. In Italy, large diaspora demonstrations were reported in Bologna, condemning deaths and alleged abuses by Pakistani security forces and expressing support for the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC). In UK, protests have also taken place outside Pakistani diplomatic premises, with Britain based Kashmiris highlighting alleged human-rights violations in PoJK. Earlier, the Awami Action Committee had called on Kashmiris worldwide to hold demonstrations today to draw international attention to the atrocities committed by the Pakistani establishment in the region. Meanwhile, the situation in PoJK remains tense, with protesters raising questions about recent controversial elections conducted under the influence of Pakistani force, targetted killings and forced disappearances of innocent people and supply disruptions. Jammu and Kashmir Joint Action Committee (JKJAAC) senior leader Sardar Shabir has claimed that around 100 people had been killed by Pakistani forces during the unrest in the occupied territory. Protests in PoJK have continued for more than two months, with demonstrators raising various demands.

national_raw_news.title: UNSC links Delhi Red Fort suicide car bombing to Al-Qaida in Indian Subcontinent
national_raw_news.content: A terrorism monitoring team of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) has declared the deadly Red Fort suicide car bombing in Delhi that killed 11 people the work of Al-Qaida in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS). The report by the Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team on terrorism to the Security Council said, the attack in last November was officially attributed to AQIS. The report said, AQIS continued to evolve from a fragmented group into a regional terrorist entity and it established logistics and financial networks, working in decentralised small, scattered cells instead of large units. It was also highlighted in the report that AQIS is trying to exploit Bangladesh to establish cells there. Against this backdrop, the team warned that terrorist threats intensified in South Asia. AQIS was founded in 2014 by Al-Qaida leader Ayman al-Zawahiri. Based in New York, Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team comprises ten experts who track global terrorism threats from those groups and their affiliates and provide periodic reports and updates to help the committees decide on groups and individuals to be sanctioned for terror related activities. An earlier report by the team released in February said Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) was reported to be linked to an attack on the Red Fort, and the new report appears to directly pin the blame on AQIS. According to the Committee, JeM has had close ties with Al-Qaida.

national_raw_news.title: Iran refutes President Trump’s claim of seizing Strait of Hormuz
national_raw_news.content: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi today rejected US President Donald Trump’s claim that Washington has total control over the Strait of Hormuz. In a social media post, Mr. Araghchi accused the US of repeatedly making miscalculations over the strategic waterway due to intelligence failures. The remarks came after Mr Trump claimed that the United States has total control over the Strait of Hormuz and would retain it. He also claimed that Iran’s military infrastructure had been severely degraded. Iran has rejected Mr. Trump claims, saying that the strategic waterway remains blocked and will not be reopened until Tehran’s conditions are accepted.

national_raw_news.title: Commonwealth Fencing: Indian team dominates with 35 medals comprising 13 gold 13 Aug 2026 | 8:30 PM 721
national_raw_news.content: India emerged as the overall champions at the Commonwealth Fencing Championship by winning an impressive 35 medals after four days of competition held at Lagos in Nigeria. Indian contingent secured thirteen gold, eight silver, and fourteen bronze medals at the event across the Under 23 and senior competitions. The senior Indian fencers claimed five gold medals in six events on the fourth and final day of the competition, securing honours in Men’s Sabre, Women’s Sabre, Men’s E’pée, Women’s Epée and Women’s foil, as well as a silver in Men’s foil. The performance also helped India win the Wilkinson Sword Trophy, awarded by the Commonwealth Fencing Federation to the country with the best overall results. Secretary-general, Fencing Association of India, Rajeev Mehta, said in a statement that lifting the Commonwealth Overall Championship title for the first time is a testament to the talent, discipline, and hard work within Indian fencing.

national_raw_news.title: Canadian Open Tennis: Men’s and women’s semifinals locked in 13 Aug 2026 | 6:37 PM 471
national_raw_news.content: In Canadian Open Tennis, second seed Elena Rybakina will take on seventh seed Iga Swiatek in Women’s Singles title clash at Toronto tomorrow. Kazakhstan’s Rybakina defeated fourth seeded American Coco Gauff by 5-7,6-2,6-2 while Polish player Swiatek overpowered Elina Svitolina of Ukraine by 6-3,1-6, 6-3 in the semi-finals today. In Men’s Singles, defending champion Ben Shelton will face Brandon Nakashima in an All American final at Montreal tomorrow. Fifth seed Shelton secured a 6-2, 6-3 victory over fellow American and 12th seed Learner Tien while 28th seed Nakashima beat Spanish teenager and 20th seed Rafael Jodar 7-6(3) 6-4 to reach his first Masters 1000 final.

national_raw_news.title: Brandon Nakashima and Ben Shelton reach Canadian Open final in Montreal 13 Aug 2026 | 10:21 AM 165
national_raw_news.content: In Canadian Open Tennis, American Brandon Nakashima defeated Spain’s Rafael Jodar 7-6(3) 6-4 in the Men’s Singles semi-finals at Montreal, this morning to reach ‌the Canadian Open final. This puts the American one win away from his first Masters 1000 title ahead of the ⁠U.S. Open. In the other semifinal, defending champion Ben Shelton has reached the finals in Montreal after defeating fellow American Learner Tien 6-2, 6-3 this morning. Shelton, who has yet to drop a single set in his entire title defense campaign, will face countryman Brandon Nakashima for the Masters 1000 trophy. In the Women’s Singles, fourth seed Coco Gauff defeated second seed Elena Rybakina in a grueling 2-hour and 50-minute blockbuster semifinal in Toronto this morning, winning 6-4, 6-7(8), 7-6(3). In another semi-final match, seventh seed Iga Świątek defeated ninth seed Elina Svitolina with a score of 6-3, 1-6, 6-3 in Toronto this morning.

national_raw_news.title: Country’s exports register robust growth of over 13% in July 13 Aug 2026 | 8:45 PM 145
national_raw_news.content: The country’s total exports, including merchandise and services are estimated at 80.14 billion US dollars in July this year, registering a robust 13.3 per cent year-on-year growth. According to the provisional data released by the Commerce Ministry, the export performance was led by merchandise shipments, which jumped over 19.6 per cent to 44.24 billion US dollars from a year earlier. The growth in merchandise exports was driven by petroleum products, electronic goods, engineering goods, organic and inorganic chemicals, cotton yarn and handloom products. Country’s merchandise trade deficit widened by 31.5 per cent year-on-year to 15 billion US dollars last month. Cumulatively, merchandise exports during April to July period of the current financial year are estimated at 173.78 billion US dollars, registering an increase of 17 per cent on an annual basis.

national_raw_news.title: Asian markets in gain, and European indices show mixed response 13 Aug 2026 | 5:45 PM 106
national_raw_news.content: In the Asian markets, South Korea’s Kospi index gained almost 3.6 per cent and Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose around 1.2 per cent. Among the major European indices, Germany’s DAX was trading 0.4 per cent up, while London’s FTSE 100 dropped 0.3 per cent, when reports last came in. On economic front, United Kingdom’s real gross domestic product (GDP) is estimated to have increased by 0.4 per cent in April to June quarter of this year, down from growth of 0.6 per cent in the first quarter. Meanwhile, GDP grew by 0.3 per cent in June, after registering no growth in the previous month, according to the GDP figures released today by the Office for National Statistics.

national_raw_news.title: NITI Aayog highlights 12 priority sectors to make India a global manufacturing hub 13 Aug 2026 | 5:40 PM 133
national_raw_news.content: Vice Chairperson of NITI Aayog, Ashok Kumar Lahiri today released a report titled Key Sectors to Position India as a Global Manufacturing Hub. The report highlights 12 priority sectors that hold strong potential for global competitiveness, local value addition, job creation, and deeper integration into global supply chains. It also lays down a strategic roadmap to strengthen India’s manufacturing ecosystem and support the vision of Viksit Bharat. The 12 key sectors shortlisted in the report are automobiles, electronics, steel, capital goods, defence and drones, chemicals, solar PV, textiles, pharmaceuticals and medical devices, telecom equipment, leather and footwear and food processing. Addressing the occasion, Dr Lahiri emphasized that manufacturing must play a significantly larger role to fulfill India’s long-term growth aspirations. He noted that economic development across most of the countries shows that sustained transformation is consistently driven by strong manufacturing and expanding exports. Highlighting towards the shifting international trends, Dr Lahiri stated that the global manufacturing landscape is undergoing rapid change as businesses actively seek to diversify their supply chains. He expressed confidence that the report will serve as a useful reference for policymakers, government, industry leaders, and researchers as they work together to strengthen India’s manufacturing ecosystem.

national_raw_news.title: Oil prices down 13 Aug 2026 | 5:24 PM 309
national_raw_news.content: Global crude oil prices declined today as investors assessed prospects for weaker ‌global demand this year and higher US crude stocks. Brent crude was trading 1.8 per cent down at 87 US dollars and 41 cents per barrel in intra-day trade. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 1.9 per cent down at 81 US dollars and 65 cents per barrel, when reports last came in. Meanwhile, the US commercial crude oil inventories increased by 17.4 million barrels to 424.4 million barrels in the week ended on 7th of August, according to data released by the Energy Information Administration. This marked the biggest weekly increase in oil inventories since January 2023.

national_raw_news.title: Digital Rupee for DBT under PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana to be launched in Chandigarh today 2 hours ago 61
national_raw_news.content: The Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) – Digital Rupee (e₹) for Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) will be launched in the Union Territory of Chandigarh today. The initiative marks the next evolution by the Government of India in welfare delivery – from physical distribution of subsidised foodgrains to Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) and now to purpose-bound digital delivery through CBDC. Quoting official sources, our correspondent reports that Chandigarh will be the first Union Territory in the country to undertake a full-fledged roll-out of CBDC-based DBT for food subsidy under Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) beneficiaries. The launch will be presided over by the Punjab Governor and Administrator, U.T. Chandigarh, Gulab Chand Kataria. Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will be the Chief Guest. Union Minister of Education, Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, Pralhad Joshi will be the Special Guest. Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Nimuben Jayantibhai Bambhaniya, besides other dignitaries from the centre and the state, would also be present. The CBDC-based initiative would also be virtually launched for Dadra and Nagar Haveli from Chandigarh.

national_raw_news.title: Nation celebrates 80th Independence Day by organising Tiranga rallies 13 Aug 2026 | 9:51 PM 76
national_raw_news.content: In Maharashtra , in the run up to India’s 80th Independence Day, nearly 1500 cadets from schools and colleges across Mumbai marched across the city’s Fort area today, showcasing a celebration of patriotism, youth power and national pride. The rally was part of NCC Maharashtra’s Independence Day campaign, where the cadets belonging to Army, Naval and Air Wings, marched to the tunes of Vande Mataram while waving the Tiranga and spirited chants of “Bharat Mata Ki Jai”. According to an official press release, NCC Maharashtra is holding rallies and community outreach programmes across all districts. The cadets are also actively supporting national campaigns like Anti-Drug awareness and TB-Mukt Bharat, alongside environmental protection, cleanliness, fitness, community development and social responsibility initiatives. In Jammu and Kashmir , a Tiranga rally was organised today. The rally commenced from District Sports Stadium Kathua and culminated at District Police Lines Kathua. Deputy Commissioner and Senior Superintendent of Police along with several officers participated in the event. Students from schools, along with prominent citizens, participated enthusiastically in the rally. Carrying the Tricolour, participants raised patriotic slogans and conveyed a message of unity and devotion to the nation. A special highlight was the participation of students in three impressive human formations. The first formation depicted 150, marking 150 years of Vande Mataram. The second represented INDIA, while the third depicted 80, highlighting 80 years of Independence. The rally witnessed enthusiastic public participation and reflected the collective spirit of Kathua in celebrating the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign and the forthcoming Independence Day. In Arunachal Pradesh, a grand Tiranga rally was organised today at Deomali as part of the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign and Independence Day celebrations, witnessing enthusiastic and overwhelming participation from the public. The event featured an energetic bikers’ rally. A 150-metre-long National Flag was carried with pride by students from the General Ground to the NCI Bridge. Similar Tiranga Abhiyaan rally was organised in Khonsa.
